chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does a man recite (the Quran) in the first and Asr prayers behind the Imam, while he does not know that the Imam is reciting? He said: 'It is not proper for him to recite; he should leave it to the Imam.'

key_terms.يَكِلُهُ إِلَى اَلْإِمَامِ: Leave it to the Imam (referring to the act of recitation)

ai.seo_question: Should a worshipper recite Quran behind the Imam during silent prayers if he doesn't know if the Imam is reciting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Qira'ah khalf al-Imam* (recitation behind the Imam) in the two-rak'ah silent prayers, specifically addressing the scenario where the worshipper is unaware of the Imam's status. The Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that it is not appropriate for the follower to recite independently if he cannot confirm the Imam is reciting, thereby emphasizing the principle of following the Imam's lead to maintain congregational unity and avoid redundancy.
